notes: design-system is the merged UI authority (absorbed the former ui-ux-pro-max and ui-styling skills). Its durable output is a portable docs/DESIGN.md (Google's open DESIGN.md format: YAML tokens + rationale), authored/updated via an open-or-join input-contract and validated by a contrast linter (designmd_lint.py). Four moves: Decide (style/color/font selection + UX/accessibility, GROUNDED by the bundled CSV corpus, not retrieved as final), Define (encode as DESIGN.md YAML tokens with an on-<X> for every surface), Validate (lint-pass is the gate), Build (shadcn/ui + Tailwind, React-only, reading tokens FROM docs/DESIGN.md). Evals cover a Decide-track positive, a Define+Build-track positive, a DESIGN.md-authoring positive, and the genuine non-fire boundary. The merge INVERTED the old design-system boundary case: style/palette/typography selection now belongs to this skill and must fire. Secondary partial boundary: for Vue / React Native / Flutter the Decide/Define/Validate moves still apply but the shadcn/Tailwind Build guidance must be withheld.

evals.prompt: Help me choose a style, color palette, and font pairing for a healthcare patient dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Fires and works the Decide move. Uses the product-type style guide (healthcare: clean/accessible, soft teal + white, Lato/Source Sans) or the bundled scripts (search.py grounding) to recommend a style, a WCAG-compliant palette expressed as semantic tokens, and a heading/body font pairing — verifying 4.5:1 contrast in both light and dark mode, designing the light/dark variants together, and steering clear of the AI anti-patterns (mesh/aurora gradients, glassmorphism-everywhere, bento grids, emoji as icons). Treats the corpus as grounding, not a frozen final answer. Must NOT defer this to another skill.

evals.prompt: Set up a three-layer design token system with CSS variables for our Next.js app, then wire it into the Tailwind theme and add dark mode with shadcn/ui.
evals.expected_output: Fires and chains the Define and Build moves. Produces primitive -> semantic -> component token layers as CSS variables (no raw hex in components), an 8pt spacing scale and typography scale, a tailwind.config mapping tokens via hsl(var(--token)) with darkMode class, and dark mode via a next-themes ThemeProvider plus toggle — using purpose-mapped dark values rather than inverted colors, pairing every themed element with a dark: variant, and testing contrast independently in both modes. Recognizes docs/DESIGN.md as the token source of truth and routes detail to tokens.md and implementation.md instead of inlining everything.

evals.prompt: Author a DESIGN.md for our fintech budgeting app and make sure it passes the linter.
evals.expected_output: Fires and runs the DESIGN.md authoring flow. Applies the open-or-join input-contract (authors docs/DESIGN.md since none exists), scaffolds it with search.py --design-system --format designmd, fills the rationale (why each token), gives every surface color an on-<X> foreground and adds a dark: override map, then VALIDATES with scripts/designmd_lint.py until 0 critical findings — verifying WCAG contrast in light and dark. Writes the result to docs/DESIGN.md (project-level, living), not a stream folder, and never resurrects the retired MASTER.md.

evals.prompt: Design the database schema and REST API for our orders service.
evals.expected_output: Should not fire. Pure backend logic, API design, and database schema work are explicitly out of scope — nothing here changes how a feature looks, feels, moves, or is interacted with, which is this skill's decision criterion.
